A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Depth Any Camera work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison, including relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original zero-shot depth-estimation experiments, component and training-data ablations, and qualitative comparisons in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative comparisons, including Tables 2–8.

M1.justification: DAC retains pitch-aware ERP conversion, FoV alignment, multi-resolution training, iDisc, and the SIlog objective. The unit-sphere formulation and new KB/MEI appendix elaborate the existing distortion-conversion component; they do not establish a different underlying method.

E1.justification: Training retains HM3D, Taskonomy, Hypersim, DDAD, and LYFT. Evaluation retains Matterport3D, Pano3D-GV2, ScanNet++, KITTI360, NYUv2, and KITTI, including the existing alternative-image-representation scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain UniDepth, Metric3Dv2, iDisc, and their existing backbone and ablation variants. Newly cited works, including 360MonoDepth, are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated data selections, metrics, training iterations, batch sizes, backbones, test resolutions, and baseline evaluation adjustments remain unchanged. The new camera-model appendix supplies implementation detail without documenting a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component, backbone, training-dataset, pitch-augmentation, and image-representation analyses in Tables 3–4 and 6–8. The qualitative examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for performance. The descriptive pitch-dispersion statistics in Table 1 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 retain the same result entries and numerical values. For example, Table 2 reports DAC delta-1 accuracy of 0.7727 on Matterport3D and 0.8517 on ScanNet++ in both versions. The qualitative result images also match.

T1.justification: New supplemental Section 8 supplies KB and MEI distortion/projection equations and derives a unit-sphere formulation that avoids division by a near-zero cosine at extreme viewing angles. This is a localized mathematical addition; the existing ERP, FoV-alignment, and lookup-table derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: perspective-only training for generalization across camera types, the same principal components, and improvements of up to 50% in delta-1 accuracy. Rewriting emphasizes the existing distortion-simulation rationale.

C2.justification: New Section 8.1 identifies numerical instability near a 180-degree FoV, and Section 8.2 explains the MEI shift parameter's role in handling larger FoVs. Section 5.2 also drops the statement that the nearly 50% improvement applies to all three indoor datasets.

D1.justification: V2 documents explicit KB/MEI parameters and conversion formulas where v1 used a generic distortion function. Conversely, Section 4.1 removes the explicit instruction to scale ground-truth depth during scale augmentation. Training settings and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Ego-Exo4D, 360MonoDepth, the Kannala–Brandt camera model, and the Mei–Rives calibration model. These extend application context and camera-model attribution without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the abstract, contribution descriptions, conversion explanation, and baseline descriptions. It inserts a camera-distortion appendix section and renumbers subsequent sections, while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Captions for Figures 4–5 and Table 2 are revised, several displayed equations become inline, and Table 4 moves earlier. Appendix material and qualitative figures shift position, while figure imagery and table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit KB/MEI mappings and numerical-stability explanation make the previously abstract camera-conversion step easier to understand and reproduce. Removing the ground-truth rescaling instruction is a small documentation loss, although Section 3 and Figure 3 retain the scaling principles. Overall, v2 offers a limited documentation improvement; its empirical evidence remains unchanged.
